title: Podcast in an afternoon
promise: From a microphone recording to a published episode with a transcript, show notes and cover art.

steps.title: Record and clean up the audio
steps.why: Audacity is a full multitrack editor that costs nothing, and its noise reduction and normalize effects do most of what a beginner needs.

steps.title: Get a transcript
steps.why: Whisper runs on your own machine and is very good at speech, but it is a command-line tool, so expect some setup with Python and ffmpeg.

steps.title: Turn the transcript into show notes
steps.why: A transcript is raw material; a few minutes in a document to pull out the summary, timestamps and links is what listeners actually read.

steps.title: Make cover art
steps.why: Canva's free tier has square templates that suit podcast directories, so you can skip the blank canvas.

steps.title: Publish the episode
steps.why: Spotify for Creators hosts your audio for free and generates the RSS feed that podcast apps subscribe to.
